rationale: Published clinical and molecular genetics literature confirms that pathogenic germline variants causing Ramond-Elliott neurodevelopmental syndrome (RAMELN, OMIM #621421) strictly cluster in the 5' coding region of TRA2B upstream of an internal alternative translation start site. Functional characterization demonstrated that these 5' truncating/loss-of-function variants spare the downstream open reading frame, driving overexpression of the repressive Tra2beta-3 isoform (which lacks the N-terminal RS1 domain) and acting via a dominant-negative mechanism rather than simple haploinsufficiency. Furthermore, population databases (e.g., MARRVEL/gnomAD CNV controls) document copy number deletions of TRA2B in unaffected control individuals, corroborating that canonical loss-of-function variants or deletions outside this specific 5' hotspot do not trigger classic Ramond-Elliott syndrome.

evidence.text: In a cohort of 12 individuals from 11 unrelated families, all identified monoallelic pathogenic variants clustered in the 5' portion of TRA2B upstream of an alternative translation initiation site, causing decreased Tra2beta-1 and increased repressive Tra2beta-3 isoform expression via an apparent dominant-negative mechanism.

source.title: Clustered variants in the 5' coding region of TRA2B cause a new neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All variants clustered in the 5' part of TRA2B, upstream of an alternative translation start site responsible for the expression of the noncanonical Tra2β-3 isoform.

evidence.text: Normal population genomic databases record healthy control individuals harboring heterozygous loss of copy number variants encompassing TRA2B, confirming that standard heterozygous deletion/haploinsufficiency outside the specific 5' dominant-negative hotspot does not cause classic Ramond-Elliott syndrome.

new_directions.question_text: Do non-truncating missense variants located in the Tra2beta RRM or RS2 domains produce distinct neurodevelopmental phenotypes or remain benign/silent in humans?
new_directions.rationale: Because the established RAMELN mechanism requires escape from nonsense-mediated decay and translation of the truncated Tra2beta-3 dominant-negative isoform, downstream missense or nonsense variants might lead to conventional haploinsufficiency, which control databases indicate may be non-penetrant or mild.
